sell_sensitivity_note: BUY-only and directional produce 30x different signal volumes. Directional fires on near-certainty in-play markets (avg 0.86 price) vs BUY-only at 0.55-0.67. This is NOT a minor sensitivity — it fundamentally changes which markets the strategy enters.

timing_structure.finding: Pools fire near-simultaneously in BUY-only mode (med gap 0-3h). No temporal confirmation structure. Exception: score_axis BUY-only shows Pool A (excess_hr) fires 2.8h before Pool B (consistency). For cross-pool to be a useful sequential signal, the gap needs to be 4-24h.
timing_structure.implication: The hypothesis of 'Pool A fires, then we wait for Pool B to confirm' is not supported. Both pools enter the same market within minutes of each other.

cross_pool_vs_single_pool.buy_only: Cross-pool reduces signal count by ~98% vs single-pool N=1 (12 vs 741). HR improvement: +16-56pp excess vs +35pp single-pool N=1. Cross-pool is better quality but catastrophically lower volume.
cross_pool_vs_single_pool.directional: Score-axis cross-pool (+54.6pp excess) beats single-pool N=2 directional (+38.8pp excess) by 16pp at similar volume (239 vs 552 signals). This is the real finding: score-axis pool construction outperforms single-pool N=2 confirmation.

knowledge_captures: Cross-pool BUY-only signal volume scales as K^2 / (market_count) — splitting K=100 into 2xK=50 reduces cross-pool overlap to ~1.6% of K=100 N=1 volume.
Score-axis pool construction (excess_hr vs consistency_sharpe) achieves Jaccard=0 and delivers 16pp higher HR than random split in directional mode — captures genuinely independent skill dimensions.
Sports YES directional mode fires predominantly on in-play near-certainty markets (avg price 0.85-0.90). Always apply hold>=4h filter to remove in-play contamination.
Cross-pool confirmation does not provide sequential timing advantage in Sports — pools fire within minutes of each other due to fast market resolution (~3h hold time).
